subject: HelixHealth evaluation: MAP, exit gates & acceptance test plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed MAP & acceptance tests for HelixHealth eval

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is an initial mutual action plan (MAP) and a lightweight acceptance-test catalog to help HelixHealth run a focused evaluation over the next 4 weeks. High level: my goal here is to make success measurable so we can get to a confident commit, or quickly surface any blockers.

Quick summary of the proposed MAP (high level milestones):
- Week 0 (kickoff): onboarding, dataset access, test owner alignment, runbook review.
- Week 1 (smoke + functional): run smoke tests + core feature validation with sample traffic.
- Week 2 (perf & edgecases): run latency/throughput tests and edge-case scenarios.
- Week 3 (security & compliance): evidence collection (logs, data retention, KMS proof) and SOC2 questionnaire check.
- Week 4 (handover & sign-off): final pass/fail decision and initial cutover plan.

Proposed acceptance tests (short):
- Intent/NER accuracy: >= 92% F1 on curated test set.
- Ranking/concordance: top-1 match rate >= 88% vs manual labels.
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms on representative load.
- Robustness: pass 90% of negative / adversarial probes in the sample set.
- Reliability: no errors > 0.5% sustained over 1 hour load test.

Exit gates (what must be green to move forward):
1) Demo + smoke tests validated by clinical PO.
2) Perf & accuracy thresholds met on representative data.
3) Security evidence provided and procurement terms acknowledged.
4) Commercial terms agreed (deal id HLX-2026-0423).

I've attached MAP_Helix_v1.xlsx and acceptance_tests_v1.md. Please review and tell me what we should change — owners, thresholds, or timelines. If this looks good, we can propose a short working session Tuesday to lock owners and the test-set.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
 jordan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122

Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & acceptance tests for HelixHealth eval

Jordan —

Thanks for this. Overall the structure looks good and I appreciate the specificity. A couple of clarifying items from our side before we lock the MAP:

1) Can you call out whether the latency targets are measured including model warmup and KV cache hit conditions? For our clinical UX the p50 must be stable under cold-start profiles too.
2) On the accuracy metrics: who provides the labeled test set? We can provide a curated ground-truth set (~1k samples) but want to confirm how Redwood will score concordance and whether there are nondeterministic sampling differences we should account for.
3) Security/compliance: we need a short checklist of artifacts (e.g., SOC2 evidence pages, retention policy, KMS key rotation notes) so our security team can pre-review.
4) Procurement: please loop procurement — our contact is procurement@helixhealth.com (cc'd if needed).

I can join a Tuesday working session; prefer 11am PT. Also — if you can add an explicit fail/escape clause (e.g., what happens if perf is borderline) that will help internal sign-off.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Director, Clinical Operations
HelixHealth

Hi Marta —

Great questions. Quick answers and a more explicit pass/fail & remediation plan below. I've also attached a concise acceptance_tests_v1.md that maps each test to owner, test harness, and timebox.

1) Latency measurement: we measure both cold-start and steady-state. Acceptance targets are for steady-state with warm cache by default; if HelixHealth needs cold-start to be part of the gate we can add p50_cold < 200ms as an additional requirement. Please confirm.

2) Labeled test-set: HelixHealth provides the ground-truth set. Redwood will run blinded scoring and return the full confusion matrix and per-intent breakdown. We will also snapshot model version + seed and publish reproducible eval artifacts so results can be audited.

3) Security artifacts: short checklist included in the attachment: SOC2 report pointer (redacted), encryption-at-rest architecture, KMS integration notes, data retention & deletion flow, and sample audit log. That should be sufficient for your initial review.

4) Fail / escape clause (proposal):
- If perf/accuracy is within 3% of the threshold at Week 2 => move to remediation sprint (2 business days) with prioritized fixes and re-run.
- If perf/accuracy misses by >3% => classify as fail; pause rollout and schedule an engineering deep-dive with HelixHealth in the following week.
- Any security/compliance gap => block until evidence is provided / mitigations accepted.

Acceptance tests (compact):
- Smoke: basic end-to-end flows for 10 canonical cases (owner: Camila, timebox: 1 day)
- Functional: intent extraction/NER scoring vs provided test-set (owner: HelixHealth lead + Redwood QA, timebox: 3 days)
- Perf: p50/p95 measurements under defined load profile (owner: Redwood infra, timebox: 1 day)
- Edge-case robustness: adversarial probes & low-resource examples (owner: Redwood product, timebox: 2 days)
- Security: SOC2 pointer, retention policy, KMS sample key (owner: Redwood security, timebox: 3 days)

I'll be present on the Tuesday call to go through the attached test catalog and to confirm owners.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com
